title: Problem
description: The one error model of the SDK: a problem details object (RFC 9457), served over REST with media type `application/problem+json` and raised in Python as an exception that carries the same members. An error caused by an authored file names that file (`layer`) and the field in it (`field`), so the user is pointed at the YAML they wrote, not at the composed document.

type.description: A URI reference identifying the kind of problem. This contract defines `urn:protodirsig:problem:compose` (a recipe does not compose), `urn:protodirsig:problem:admission` (a submission failed admission), `urn:protodirsig:problem:not-found` (an unknown id or name), `urn:protodirsig:problem:invalid-request` (a request body that does not match its schema, or a request the SDK cannot act on as given) and `urn:protodirsig:problem:execution` (an accepted run failed while executing; status 500).

title.description: A short, human-readable summary of the kind of problem. It is the same for every occurrence of a `type`.

status.description: The HTTP status code of the response: 422 for composition, validation and admission errors, 404 for an unknown id or name, 500 for a run that failed while executing.

detail.description: A human-readable explanation of this occurrence, written for the user who has to fix it.

instance.description: A URI reference identifying this occurrence, for example the request path.

layer.description: The authored file at fault, relative to the library root, for example `scenarios/tahoe_static_pose.yaml` or `manifold_sensors/auror-nir.yaml`. Null when no single file is at fault.

field.description: The field at fault within `layer`, as a dotted path with list indices in brackets, for example `fidelity` or `sensors[1]`. Null when the whole file is at fault (for example, it does not parse) or no field can be named.

errors.description: For a sweep that failed admission: one entry per run that failed, each naming the run and the authored file and field at fault. A sweep is admitted as a whole, so every failing run is reported at once.

layer.description: The authored file at fault, relative to the library root, or null.

field.description: The field at fault within `layer`, or null.
